newsitem.title: UK: IBCA downgrades Turkey foreign currency rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA downgrades Turkey foreign currency rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Friday it downgraded the long-term foreign currency rating of all senior and unsecured debt issues of the Republic of Turkey to B plus from BB minus.

IBCA said the rating applies to some $50 billion of public and publicly guaranteed foreign currency debt. A short-term foreign currency rating of B continues to apply to issues of up to one year, it said.
"IBCA acknowledges that the Turkish economy has many private sector strengths which would ordinarily justify a higher rating towards the upper end of the BB range," it said in a statement.
"However, these attributes continue to be undermined by economic mismanagement and a lack of political will to tackle public sector reforms."

IBCA said the collapse of the centre-right Tansu Ciller administration in September 1995 ushed in nine months of political and economic uncertainty during which the economy drifted for lack of a stable government.

"The subsequent appointment of Turkey's first pro-Islamist led administration -- the Refah-Yol coalition -- has not done nearly enough to arrest this policy drift and serious macro-economic imbalances have continued to develop," it said.
"Inflation, the fiscal deficit and the current account deficit all now rival or exceed the leveals prevailing at the time of the last crisis in 1993-94."
